A fresh check found these problems in this version. Fix each one, and keep everything that is right:
- Card, wording: "√10 is not a whole number, so it is irrational" gives the wrong reason. Many numbers that are not whole are rational, such as 3/4 or 2.6363..., and the card itself says so. rejected.title: Rational and irrational numbers
card: Rational
a number that can be written as a fraction of two integers, such as 3/4 or 5/1. Whole numbers, negative integers such as −6 and fractions such as −2/3 are all rational.
Irrational
a number that cannot be written as a fraction of two integers. Examples are π and √2.

The decimal of an irrational number never ends and never repeats in a pattern. The decimal of a rational number either ends or repeats, and any decimal that ends or repeats can be written as a fraction.
For a whole number, its square root is rational only when the number is a perfect square. √49 = 7, which is 7/1, so it is rational. √10 is not a whole number, so it is irrational.
rejected.remember: If it can be a fraction of integers, it is rational. If its decimal never ends or repeats, it is irrational.

a.q: Which of these numbers is irrational?
a.why: 7 is a whole number but not a perfect square, so √7 is irrational and its decimal never ends or repeats. √81 = 9 = 9/1, 0.25 = 1/4 and −6 = −6/1 are all fractions of integers, so they are rational.
a.clue: Try to write each number as a fraction of two integers.

b.q: Mia says a number is irrational because its decimal has many digits. Her calculator shows 2.636363... with the 63 repeating. What is true?
opts: It is rational, because a repeating decimal is a fraction
It is irrational, because the decimal is very long
It is irrational, because it is not a whole number
It is rational, because it has only two repeating digits
b.why: A decimal that repeats in a pattern can be written as a fraction of two integers, so the number is rational. In fact 2.636363... = 29/11. Length does not matter, and neither does how many digits repeat: an irrational decimal must never repeat at all.
b.clue: Does the decimal repeat in a pattern or not?
